Fairy-Tale Villains Rules

Every player is a villain with an own goal. Whoever reaches it first wins – while the others send heroes into the way.

The rules

Domain
Each villain has a domain of four places, each with two or three actions, and a goal card that shows the goal and what is still missing.
A turn
Move your figure to another place of your domain and use its actions, each once, in any order. At the end of the turn you draw back up to 4 cards.
Actions
Gold: take that much gold. Play a card: pay its cost. Discard cards: as many as you like. Move: move one of your helpers or a hero in your domain to another place. Defeat: remove a hero anywhere in your domain. Twist of the tale: see below. Goal action: the step towards your goal that can be done at this place.
Cards
Helpers stay at the place where they were played and lower the price of defeating heroes there by their strength. Tricks work once. Every villain has two cards of its own: one does the goal action from anywhere, the other makes a hero disappear.
Heroes
A hero blocks his place: its actions can't be used, only the hero himself can be defeated there. Defeating costs his strength in gold, minus the strength of your helpers at his place.
Twist of the tale
Choose another villain and draw two cards from their twist pile. Put one of them into their domain: a hero on a free place of your choice, or an event that happens at once (such as losing gold). The other card is discarded.
Start and prices
The first player starts with no gold, the second with 1, the third with 2, the fourth with 3. What the goal steps cost depends a little on the number of players, so that every villain has about the same chance; the goal card always shows the prices of the current game.
Playing
Tap a place to move there; the buttons below show its actions. For a card, tap it in your hand first, then Play a card. Choices (which hero, which twist card, where to) appear as buttons in a box. Tap another villain's line to see their whole domain. The log shows the last moves, including the computer's.

The six villains

The Gingerbread Witch
Builds three gingerbread houses in the Bakehouse and then heats the Oven. Heroes: Hansel, Gretel, the woodcutter, the white duck and the little white bird.
The Big Bad Wolf
Eats chalk to soften his voice, gets dough and flour on his paw at the Mill, knocks at the Goats' House and then must end a turn in the Dark Forest. Heroes: the mother goat, the youngest kid, the hunter, Little Red Cap and the grandmother.
Rumpelstiltskin
Collects gold – also by spinning straw into gold – and must end a turn with enough of it while the Messenger, who found out his name, is not in his domain. Heroes: the queen, the king, the messenger, the miller and a guard.
The Wicked Stepmother
Brings the three gifts – laces, comb and apple – to the Dwarfs' Cottage, one after the other, and then asks the mirror. Heroes: Snow White, the kind huntsman, a dwarf, the prince and the seven dwarfs.
The Sorcerer in the Tower
Catches four birds on the Bird Meadow, at most one per turn. Heroes: Joringel, Jorinde, the shepherd, the blood-red flower and the nightingale.
The Thorn Fairy
Lets the thorn hedge grow at all four places of her domain. Heroes: the king's son (he also cuts down a hedge), the king's daughter, the old king, the cook and the twelfth wise woman.

Example

A domain of four places. The figure stands on the second place; a hero with strength 3 blocks the fourth. A helper with strength 1 stands there too, so defeating the hero costs only 2 gold.
